# hyperfluid_sql_engine_cluster (Resource)

A SQL engine cluster (Trino) in an environment. Its catalogs are `hyperfluid_sql_engine_catalog` resources.

~> Changing `env` or `name` deletes the cluster and the catalogs it serves.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "hyperfluid_env" "default" {
  name = "default"
}

resource "hyperfluid_sql_engine_cluster" "analytics" {
  env             = data.hyperfluid_env.default.id
  name            = "analytics"
  description     = "Reporting queries"
  worker_replicas = 2
  worker_memory   = "4GB"

  worker_auto_scaling = {
    enabled      = true
    min_replicas = 2
    max_replicas = 6
  }

  expose_to_internet = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `env` (String) Environment id the cluster runs in. Changing this forces a new cluster.
- `name` (String) Cluster name, unique in the environment. Changing this forces a new cluster.
- `worker_replicas` (Number) Number of Trino workers.

### Optional

- `coordinator_cpu` (String) Coordinator CPU, as a Kubernetes quantity such as `500m`.
- `coordinator_memory` (String) Coordinator memory, such as `2GB`.
- `description` (String) Free-form description.
- `expose_to_internet` (Boolean) Whether native clients reach the cluster from outside. Left out, it is not managed (the platform exposes clusters by default).
- `hash_partition_count` (Number) Trino `query.hash-partition-count`.
- `max_memory_per_node` (String) Memory one query may use on a node, such as `3GB`.
- `query_max_execution_time` (String) Longest a query may run, as a Trino duration such as `1h`.
- `query_max_memory` (String) Memory one query may use across the cluster, such as `2GB`.
- `refresh_interval` (Number) Seconds between two refreshes of the catalog metadata the console shows.
- `task_concurrency` (Number) Trino `task.concurrency`.
- `worker_auto_scaling` (Attributes) Scale the workers between two bounds on their load. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--worker_auto_scaling))
- `worker_cpu` (String) Worker CPU, as a Kubernetes quantity such as `500m`.
- `worker_memory` (String) Worker memory, such as `2GB`.

### Read-Only

- `host` (String) External host, empty when not exposed.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `port` (Number) External port.
- `status` (String) Current status, such as `Online` or `Sleeping`.

<a id="nestedatt--worker_auto_scaling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `worker_auto_scaling`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether autoscaling is on.
- `max_replicas` (Number) Most workers.
- `min_replicas` (Number) Fewest workers.

Optional:

- `target_cpu_utilization` (Number) Average worker CPU utilization to aim for, in percent.
- `target_memory_utilization` (Number) Average worker memory utilization to aim for, in percent.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# SQL engine cluster import id is the cluster id.
terraform import hyperfluid_sql_engine_cluster.analytics 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
